news.title: Trump says he was 'kidding' about Dana White press secretary offer
news.summary: The president told the Ultimate Fighting Championship boss to "please take the job" in a Truth Social post on Saturday.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Trump says he was 'kidding' about Dana White press secretary offer
news.summaryTr: The president told the Ultimate Fighting Championship boss to "please take the job" in a Truth Social post on Saturday.
news.articleText: Trump says he was 'kidding' about Dana White press secretary offer - Published US President Donald Trump has said he "was kidding" about asking Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) boss Dana White to be the White House press secretary. Trump told the media on Sunday that White "loves the idea" but that the invitation was "just a little fun". It comes after the president posted on his Truth Social platform on Saturday that he had offered White the role, asking him to take it while writing, "Dana will be a Press Secretary like none other." White said later that day he was going to meet the president on Monday, but would not be drawn into whether or not he would take the vacant position. On Sunday Trump told reporters White was visiting him on Monday for "other reasons". "I think he's going to be in Washington. So he's going to come over and see me. "I will tell you, I was only kidding. But Dana loves the idea. And there's only one Dana. He's great," the president said. "But, it was it was just a little fun." The press secretary role is yet to be filled after it became vacant in October when Katie Zacharia quit after less than five days in the job. She took over from Karoline Leavitt, who was the youngest press secretary in US history and had held the role since Trump began his second term. Trump's job offer came after a heavy loss in the midterm elections, where the Republican Party lost its majority in both houses of Congress. In his Truth Social post on Saturday, he said he was "pleased to announce" that White "has been offered the job". He said he had asked White to bring with him several current and former mixed martial arts fighters as "assistants". "We need these people to defend us against the Lunatic Left," he wrote. "Dana, please take the job!" Asked about the Trump offer at a news conference on Saturday, the UFC chief executive said he had "lot of jobs already". "I'm sure we'll have something to talk about after that," he said of their planned Monday meeting, but did not say whether or not he would take the job. White leads UFC, and PowerSlap, a regulated slap-fighting promotion league, as well as recently launching promotion company Zuffa Boxing. He is also a board member of Meta, the owner of Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp. White appeared as a speaker in support of Trump's White House campaigns at the Republican National Conventions in 2016, 2020 and 2024. He also appeared on stage for Trump's victory speech in the 2024 presidential election. This summer, the UFC staged a cage match on the White House lawn.

news.summary: Investors pulled a net $1.21 billion from BlackRock’s IBIT last week as Bitcoin fell below $76,000 and US technology stocks sold off.

news.titleTr: Bitcoin ETFs shed $1.3B in biggest weekly outflow since late June
news.summaryTr: Investors pulled a net $1.21 billion from BlackRock’s IBIT last week as Bitcoin fell below $76,000 and US technology stocks sold off.
news.articleText: Bitcoin ETFs shed $1.3B in biggest weekly outflow since late June Investors pulled a net $1.21 billion from BlackRock’s IBIT last week as Bitcoin fell below $76,000 and US technology stocks sold off. US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) recorded $1.28 billion in net outflows last week, their largest weekly withdrawals since late June. The withdrawals brought the funds’ net outflows for the year to about $919 million, according to SoSoValue. The funds had already posted $515 million in net outflows in October. Bitcoin fell below $76,000 last week as traders digested the fallout from Binance’s $6.3 billion hack, uncertainty after the US midterm elections and a sell-off in technology stocks. BlackRock’s IBIT leads Bitcoin ETF outflows BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT), the world’s largest spot Bitcoin ETF by assets, recorded $1.21 billion in net outflows last week, according to Farside Investors data. The withdrawals extended IBIT’s losing streak to six consecutive trading sessions, with approximately $1.44 billion pulled from the fund since Oct. 30. IBIT accounted for about 95% of the weekly total reported by SoSoValue. IBIT recorded net outflows for six consecutive trading sessions through Friday, bringing withdrawals since Oct. 30 to about $1.44 billion. Fidelity’s Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund (FBTC) drew about $93 million in net inflows for the week, despite losing nearly $200 million Thursday. Bitfire flags further downside risk for Bitcoin Shifting expectations for US interest rates, uncertainty after the midterms and weakness in technology stocks weighed on crypto markets, Bitfire Research said in a statement shared with Cointelegraph. Bitfire said investors were also reassessing whether Congress could pass the CLARITY Act before year-end. Related: Bitcoin price dips under $75K as crypto markets miss tech-stock rebound Bitfire cited a Crypto Fear & Greed Index reading of 25 and a negative Coinbase Premium, which indicates Bitcoin was trading at a discount on Coinbase relative to the indicator’s benchmark. Bitfire described the market as being in a “breakdown and bottom-seeking phase,” pointing to upcoming US inflation data and signals from the Federal Reserve as factors to watch. It said that a sustained break below the $74,400–$75,000 support range could lead to further selling. Bitcoin traded at $74,049 at publication, below the lower end of that range. It was down 5% over seven days and 2.3% over 24 hours, according to CoinGecko. Magazine: Vitalik ‘pivots’ ETH to store of value, crypto suffers after US midterms: Hodler’s Digest

news.title: At least 34 dead after Europe-bound migrant boat sinks off Senegal
news.summary: The Atlantic crossing to Spain's Canary Islands remains dangerous for migrants seeking a better life
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: At least 34 dead after Europe-bound migrant boat sinks off Senegal
news.summaryTr: The Atlantic crossing to Spain's Canary Islands remains dangerous for migrants seeking a better life
news.articleText: At least 34 dead after Europe-bound migrant boat sinks off Senegal - Published At least 34 people have died after a boat carrying migrants sank off the coast of Senegal, the Senegalese Press Agency (APS) reports, citing an official source. The Interior ministry said one person had been rescued, but the number of people still missing was yet to be established. The small wooden boat capsized between the capital, Dakar and the northern city of Saint-Louis, as it headed towards Spain's Canary Islands. Spanish migrant rights group Walking Borders recorded 635 deaths on the Atlantic route to the Canary Islands between January and May 2026, the highest toll among the routes it monitors. Saliou Diouf, founder of Senegalese migrant aid group Boza Fii, told AFP that all the bodies recovered so far were Senegalese. The nationalities of other people on board was yet to be established, as search operations continued. President Bassirou Diomaye Faye has expressed his condolences to the victims' families and urged Senegalese nationals not risk their lives on the dangerous sea crossings. In a statement posted on X, he pledged to intensify efforts to dismantle the networks organising the journeys. "We will relentlessly continue the fight against those who organise these crossings and the work that gives our young people reasons to hope here," he said. The tragedy comes amid renewed concerns over the dangers facing migrant attempting to reach Europe by sea. Walking Borders estimates that about 21 people died for every 100 who reached the Canary Islands during the period it monitored. Senegalese authorities said they had intercepted another boat, on Friday, carrying 142 migrants attempting to reach Spain. Those on board included 23 women, two babies and two other children. Police said the group comprised nationals of Senegal, Gambia, Guinea-Bissau, Guinea and Nigeria. Meanwhile, a state of emergency was declared on the Spanish island of El Hierro on Saturday following a surge in migrant arrivals. More than 3,300 people have reached the island in about 30 boats since the beginning of November, according to local authorities. The Canary Islands have become a major entry point into Europe for migrants and refugees making the dangerous Atlantic crossing from West Africa. The route has grown in prominence amid tighter controls and increased cooperation between European countries and North African states, which may have diverted some journeys away from the central Mediterranean. Limited employment opportunities, family pressures and established migration networks are among the factors driving people to leave Senegal, according to the International Organization for Migration (IOM). For many young people, the prospect of finding work and earning more abroad remains a powerful incentive, despite the risks of crossing the Atlantic in overcrowded boat. Nearly one in four young people in Senegal was unemployed in the second quarter of 2026, according to the country's statistics agency. The figure highlights the challenge facing President Faye's government as it seeks to create jobs for a predominantly young population that overwhelmingly voted for him in the 2024 elections. In a statement on Sunday, Senegal's interior ministry said it would continue efforts to combat people-smuggling networks, including by strengthening cooperation with neighbouring countries. The Interior ministry said one person had been rescued, but the number of people still missing was yet to be established. The small wooden boat capsized between the capital, Dakar and the northern city of Saint-Louis, as it headed towards Spain's Canary Islands. Spanish migrant rights group Walking Borders recorded 635 deaths on the Atlantic route to the Canary Islands between January and May 2026, the highest toll among the routes it monitors. Saliou Diouf, founder of Senegalese migrant aid group Boza Fii, told AFP that all the bodies recovered so far were Senegalese. The nationalities of other people on board was yet to be established, as search operations continued. President Bassirou Diomaye Faye has expressed his condolences to the victims' families and urged Senegalese nationals not risk their lives on the dangerous sea crossings. In a statement posted on X, he pledged to intensify efforts to dismantle the networks organising the journeys. "We will relentlessly continue the fight against those who organise these crossings and the work that gives our young people reasons to hope here," he said. The tragedy comes amid renewed concerns over the dangers facing migrant attempting to reach Europe by sea. Walking Borders estimates that about 21 people died for every 100 who reached the Canary Islands during the period it monitored. Senegalese authorities said they had intercepted another boat, on Friday, carrying 142 migrants attempting to reach Spain. Those on board included 23 women, two babies and two other children. Police said the group comprised nationals of Senegal, Gambia, Guinea-Bissau, Guinea and Nigeria. Meanwhile, a state of emergency was declared on the Spanish island of El Hierro on Saturday following a surge in migrant arrivals. More than 3,300 people have reached the island in about 30 boats since the beginning of November, according to local authorities. The Canary Islands have become a major entry point into Europe for migrants and refugees making the dangerous Atlantic crossing from West Africa. The route has grown in prominence amid tighter controls and increased cooperation between European countries and North African states, which may have diverted some journeys away from the central Mediterranean. Limited employment opportunities, family pressures and established migration networks are among the factors driving people to leave Senegal, according to the International Organization for Migration (IOM). For many young people, the prospect of finding work and earning more abroad remains a powerful incentive, despite the risks of crossing the Atlantic in overcrowded boat. Nearly one in four young people in Senegal was unemployed in the second quarter of 2026, according to the country's statistics agency. The figure highlights the challenge facing President Faye's government as it seeks to create jobs for a predominantly young population that overwhelmingly voted for him in the 2024 elections. In a statement on Sunday, Senegal's interior ministry said it would continue efforts to combat people-smuggling networks, including by strengthening cooperation with neighbouring countries. news.summary: Jensen Huang also admitted to having been "unfaithful" to his wife and says he will cooperate with a security investigation.

news.titleTr: Nvidia launches investigation into CEO's affair with suspected Chinese spy
news.summaryTr: Jensen Huang also admitted to having been "unfaithful" to his wife and says he will cooperate with a security investigation.
news.articleText: Nvidia launches investigation into CEO's affair with suspected Chinese spy - Published US tech giant Nvidia has opened an independent investigation following reports its CEO Jensen Huang had a relationship with a suspected Chinese spy. The company, one of the most valuable in the world, said its board had no reason to believe the company's secrets or national security were compromised, adding that the CEO was committed to continuing to lead the company. Separately, Jensen Huang admitted to having been "unfaithful" to his wife and apologised for hurting her and their children. US intelligence officials believed that Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, who had a close relationship with Jensen Huang, was a spy for Beijing, according to a New York Times report. Jensen Huang said he took "full responsibility" for what he did, adding that he had fallen short of his responsibilities to Nvidia's employees, board and shareholders. Nvidia is one of the world's largest companies and seen as central to making the hardware for emerging AI technologies, and Jensen Huang has been in charge of it for more than 30 years. He said: "I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry." His statement continued: "Regarding the national security concerns raised in news reports, Nvidia's Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation. I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. "I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America's national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American." A separate statement issued by Nvidia's board of directors said it would begin an investigation in "light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort". It continued: "The Board prioritises US national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of Nvidia and its shareholders. "While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information." US President Donald Trump said he had not spoken to the Nvidia boss since news of the investigation emerged. "I just know he's a fine person, but you never know what's going on," Trump told reporters, adding that he had "done an amazing job for our country". The New York Times reported in late October that Trump had been briefed last year on intelligence alleging Alice Huang was spying on China's behalf. Asked by reporters on Sunday whether he now wished he had "acted on the intelligence" at the time, Trump responded: "No, I don't think so. I think he's an honourable guy." Secretary of State Marco Rubio, meanwhile, refused to comment when asked about Huang before flying to Paris for a meeting of the G7. Rubio told the press: "I can't comment on any of that. I just can't comment because of the nature of it. And I also can't comment on an internal corporate matter that's going on with Nvidia, as you highlight, I don't know anything about that part of it so." Last spring, the secretary of state reportedly oversaw the drafting of a memo that warned the Trump administration about Huang's relationship with the Chinese businesswoman, according to the New York Times. China has previously rejected allegations of an espionage operation targeting the Nvidia chief, describing the claims as "groundless speculation". Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun told reporters at a daily press briefing: "We have already responded to this. The allegations about Chinese spies are entirely groundless, speculative and intended to smear and malign China." Jensen Huang rescued Nvidia from bankruptcy on more than one occasion, and he took risks on AI a long time before the rest of the world did. His decision to make Nvidia chips, originally designed for gaming, become the best in the business for AI development, has now paid off in spades and the company is worth trillions. This is a big blow for a man who is renowned for being a workaholic, a perfectionist and someone who expects incredibly high standards from his staff. Alice Huang, who is of no relation to Jensen Huang, is linked to Singapore-based data centre firm Megaspeed. The company told the New York Times last month its current leadership took the allegations seriously and had appointed external legal advisers to conduct an internal investigation. Nvidia is a central player in AI infrastructure, providing chips to leading AI model developers including OpenAI and Meta. The microchip manufacturer is worth some $4.5 trillion, making it one of the most valuable companies ever. US intelligence agencies had been monitoring Alice Huang and concluded that she was acting on behalf of the Chinese government, according to unnamed sources cited by the New York Times. Surveillance reportedly revealed communications between Alice Huang and an American citizen, who was subsequently identified as Jensen Huang through a process known as "unmasking". It remains unclear what information Alice Huang – who is also known as Huang Le – allegedly passed to Beijing, how valuable it was, or when she is believed to have begun gathering intelligence. Alice Huang did not respond to the paper's request for comment. Last week, members of Congress wrote to Jensen Huang, asking him to appear before them in the light of the reported relationship. Three House Republican committee leaders asked the CEO to appear later in the month, to talk about Nvidia's "security protocols against foreign adversary espionage" given his reported relationship with Alice Huang. "Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the PRC's [China's] access to sensitive US technology and information. "The issue of PRC infiltration and access to cutting-edge US technology is core to the investigative work of our three committees this Congress," the letter said. Nvidia's AI chips have been a major focus of the rivalry between the US and China, and Washington has previously imposed controls on where its advanced products can be sold. The H200, Nvidia's second most advanced semiconductor, had previously been restricted by Washington over concerns that it would give China's technology industry an edge over the US. In January, the Trump administration said it would allow the company to sell its H200 chips to Chinese customers under certain conditions. news.title: Krakow shooting suspect has died in hospital, police say
news.summary: At least six people were killed in the shooting, and three bodies of the suspect's family members were found at their home.

news.titleTr: Krakow shooting suspect has died in hospital, police say
news.summaryTr: At least six people were killed in the shooting, and three bodies of the suspect's family members were found at their home.
news.articleText: Krakow shooting suspect has died in hospital, police say - Published A gunman suspected of killing six people in central Krakow and his parents and sister at their home has died in hospital, Polish police say. The 24-year-old, who officials said was apparently inspired by "far-right ideologies", was injured after opening fire in central Krakow, the second largest city in Poland, on Saturday. Armed officers raced to the scene and engaged in a gunfight with the suspect, who was shot within three minutes of the attack beginning, preventing a further massacre, officials said. Krakow police said the suspected gunman died early on Monday morning. After the shooting, which began shortly before 15:00 local time (14:00 GMT) in Krakow's busy Main Market Square, police identified the attacker as a 24-year-old Polish man but did not confirm his name. In the hours after the shooting, a minister said early investigations indicate he was inspired by "far-right ideologies". The minister also described him as an "ultra-nationalist" without giving further details. Six people - four women and two men - are confirmed to have been killed in the attack. Four victims are Polish, while a British national and an Austrian woman were also killed. Poland's Prime Minister Donald Tusk said three bodies - two women and one man - were found at the gunman's house when it was searched after the attack. On Sunday, Polish police confirmed those three victims had been identified as the alleged gunman's 53-year-old father, 52-year-old mother and 21-year-old sister. Polish media has reported the suspect had a firearms permit and may have obtained the weapons from his family home. Sixteen people, including five foreigners, two police officers and the attacker, were taken to hospital. The interior ministry later said they were from Austria, Britain, Germany, Portugal and Russia. Speaking on Sunday, one of the two surgeons who treated victims on the street after the attack said his colleague "undoubtedly" saved the life of a gravely injured police officer. The two surgeons, who were eating near the Main Market Square when the gunman opened fire, rushed to the scene to treat both the attacker and the two injured police officers. Professor Michal Pędziwiatr told the BBC: "We saw the shooting attack. And what a surgeon can do in a situation like this?... We decided to help the victims as soon as possible." "We rushed into the area where the shooting was and started our rescue, because there were no ambulances available, there were no professionals around." Pędziwiatr said his colleague, who has been named by local media as Dr Mateusz Wierdak, used his hand to stem the bleeding from the most severely injured policeman, allowing time for an ambulance to arrive. On Sunday it was reported that both injured officers had emerged from comas. Witnesses who were near the Main Market Square have described their panic and confusion as the attack unfolded. Ruby Catherine Warren, from London, heard gunfire and "yelled at my friends to run and we all sprinted for our lives". She said they "just kept sprinting" until they found a hotel to shelter inside. Tom Brook, from West Yorkshire, was inside a McDonald's near the square when he heard "multiple gunshots and saw people running for cover". "I then walked into the square and saw paramedics working on someone outside [a shop] and there was a dead body covered in foil blankets 20 meters away," he said. In the wake of the shooting, Poland declared the country would enter two days of national mourning. After travelling to Krakow, Tusk said: "Until now in Poland we haven't had such drastic cases of terrorism...that's what we have to call this cruel attack on people's lives here in Krakow." UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he was "shocked and saddened by the appalling shooting in Kraków". "My thoughts are with the families of those who have lost their lives, everyone injured and all those affected by this senseless violence. The United Kingdom stands in solidarity with the people of Poland," he added. Main Market Square reopened on Sunday evening after a security cordon was lifted. news.title: How you can get council's £250 cost of living help

news.titleTr: How you can get council's £250 cost of living help
news.summaryTr: Applications for household grants of up to £250 are opening to some Surrey residents.
news.articleText: How you can get council's £250 cost of living help - Published Applications for household grants of up to £250 are due to open for residents in part of Surrey. Tandridge District Council is funding the scheme, which last ran in January, to support residents with the cost of living. Who is eligible? Applicants must live in the Tandridge district, be over 16 years old and be "experiencing financial hardship", the council says. They must also prove they are struggling to pay for essential items for themselves or their dependants by submitting full bank statements for August, September and October. Other evidence such as arrears letters and energy bills can be uploaded too. Grants are available to households even if they receive support from elsewhere, such as Surrey County Council funds, external. Tandridge District Council said it aimed to provide support to those who needed help the most. How much money is available? Successful applicants will receive a one-off payment, with the soonest payment date at the end of November. Households without children can apply for £150, while those with under 18s can apply for £250. The scheme is worth a total of £150,000 and applications will be processed on a first come, first served basis, the council said. Other authorities in the county offer their own cost of living support. How do I apply? Residents can apply online, external or by phone from 10:00 GMT on 9 November. People who apply by phone will have to take their bank statements to the council's offices in Oxted. Applications close on 31 December at the latest. news.titleTr: Inside the French drug gangs recruiting children to kill
news.summaryTr: The BBC enters Marseille's dangerous underworld, where young people are trapped, brutalised and exploited.
news.articleText: Inside the French drug gangs recruiting children to kill - Published Warning: Strong language and descriptions of sexual violence Although she had just bought hashish from a drug dealer, the woman decided to call the police. It was because, along with the illegal drugs, she had been handed a note by the young seller during their brief meeting on a Marseille housing estate in 2022. "We're being held captive and need help. We are 15-years-old," it read. The teenage dealer, a French court heard earlier this year, was one of two boys being held by a gang which they had both initially approached looking for paid work - albeit illegal. One boy had been tasked with handling money, the other worked streets around the Frais-Vallon estate. Soon though, bosses had accused them of being responsible for "shortfalls" in takings. What followed were regular beatings, the court was told, and being forced to dance naked in front of a camera as a form of blackmail. One of the boys was also raped. Hours after the woman was passed the note, the two teenagers had tried to escape from a second-storey window, injuring themselves in the process. One managed to get away, while the other was caught, beaten and stabbed, but survived. Arrests were made. Photos on the phone of one of the boys' alleged torturers showed several other young men in a similarly distressed condition. Six men have since been handed hefty sentences for what happened to the two teenagers. The boys' story highlights the grip that drug gangs hold over parts of France's second city. While the blend of Mediterranean culture, street art and hip-hop scene has made Marseille a popular tourist destination - beyond the city centre, it is another story. After months of trying, a BBC team managed to enter this dangerous world - centred on deprived streets and high-rise housing estates in the port city, which police do not enter lightly. We found an environment where ruthless gangs lure vulnerable young people with promises of easy money, but end up trapping them in a world of drug dealing, brutality and exploitation. We saw how gangs use social media to recruit hitmen and spoke to several young men caught up in the violence. From prison, one gang member accused of involvement in several murders explained how his "cold-bloodedness" had helped him rise through the ranks. The city's most powerful gang, DZ Mafia, emerged victorious from a bloody turf war and is now one of the most feared criminal organisations in France. DZ is the official internet country code for Algeria, where one of the gang's founders, a French-Algerian called Mehdi Laribi, was detained earlier this year under a French arrest warrant. The criminal outfit rose to prominence in 2023, when it became the first French gang to capitalise on its notoriety by releasing video statements - using social media to market itself as a brand - says the head of the country's anti-drug trafficking unit, Dimitri Zoulas. Its most recent statement came in July, when the mayor of a nearby town had to be placed in police protection, after intelligence suggested he was in danger of being targeted by the group. In an online video, six masked men dressed in black stood behind a table - as one of them read a statement denying DZ Mafia's involvement. France's expanding illegal drugs market - which has seen a surge in cocaine imports alongside high volumes of cannabis and synthetic drugs - has also helped the gang grow rapidly. The number of cocaine users in France is expected soon to reach two million, says Zoulas, up from 600,000 in 2017. Drug smuggling across France generates €7bn (£5.9bn) a year, involving 200,000 people, he adds. Many of those distributing the drugs are children and the authorities say the number of minors caught up in trafficking is increasing. During 2025, more than 10,000 children were involved in some way, according to official figures. DZ Mafia is a prime example. To reach more customers, it needs more gang members - more children. We have found it is now recruiting young people from across France - not just to sell drugs, but to carry out kidnap, torture and murder. They are a generation seen as easy to corrupt, but also expendable, by the kingpins who typically control them from prison or overseas. And, as police and judges warn, once these children enter Marseille's underworld, it is very hard to get them out. Few know the human cost of Marseille's gangs like mother Karine Brouillard - who lives at the other end of France, almost as far from the Mediterranean coast as you can get. Her son, Hugo, first ran away aged 15 - from his home in a village in the Nord department - after an argument with his family. He was picked up by police three days later, almost 1,000km (600 miles) away in Marseille, with money and cannabis on him. He was taken home. But several years later, in 2023, Hugo planned to return south, telling his parents he had secured a holiday job at a restaurant near Marseille. "He gave regular updates," Karine remembers. "He called me, everything was going well." Three weeks later, a doctor called. Karine says she will never forget his words: "Your son arrived last night. He took a bullet to the head." Police believe Hugo was brought for medical help from a gang-controlled area and suspect he was involved with one. That area was Quartier Nord. Our best way into Quartier Nord, where DZ Mafia wields power, is with the help of resident Fadella Ouidef, a 41-year-old mother-of-four who gives us a tour. Thirty-seven seconds after entering one housing estate, we find ourselves cornered. Car horns sound the moment Fadella's Peugeot passes a gang checkpoint - the teenagers manning the post immediately spot our camera. "Wait, stop filming," Fadella warns, as a grey 4x4 forces us to the side of the road. "I'm making a report for my housing association," she tells the inquisitive driver. He eventually agrees to let us leave if we stop filming. It is unnerving to see a non-police vehicle move so assertively and a relief to watch it leave. "Lately, the gangs have been very aggressive," explains Fadella. "What we simply try to do is make sure our young people understand what's happening is wrong." Fadella speaks to a wider fear among local families: that their children are enticed by huge sums of money to take a criminal path that robs them of their innocence. Money is what led one young man to spend his teenage years with DZ Mafia. In order for our interviewees to speak freely, or because of safety concerns, we have agreed to protect their identities. Camil tells us he worked up the gang's ranks to "running security" in one area it controls. The now 20-year-old, who claims to have left the group, is highly suspicious of our presence, but agrees to tell us how the gang recruits young members. "They know how to get inside your head. Whatever you want, they give to you," he says. This can range from nice cars and spacious apartments, to drugs and prostitutes, he explains. "You feel loyalty because of what they give you. You'll stay until the very end, until either death or prison." Camil also gives a sobering assessment of what happens if the gang identifies a weakness in a recruit: "They'll exploit it. You're their bitch, it's over." DZ Mafia member, Adam - not his real name - tells us he was part of a DZ Mafia hit squad when we speak to him in a Snapchat video call. He is currently in prison awaiting trial, after being implicated in several murders. "People noticed my determination, my cold-bloodedness and, without wanting to, I climbed up the ladder of the gang," says Adam. "It became my place, I had to roll with it." During the chat, he agrees the killings he has been charged with were "quite shocking". "Attempts in broad daylight, in traffic jams… it can range from going to hit a guy, slap him to taking him in front of his mother and burning him up in a car. I think I have good composure, I handle it fairly well." We challenge Adam on whether he feels regret when carrying out such acts of brutality. He says he is "feeling in-part guilty" but claims to have no regrets. "If I hadn't done all of this, there are other people who would have done that in my place, and so on. I am just another brick in the wall," he says. Like so many teenagers from Marseille, he knew large sums of money could be earned quickly in drug trafficking. Now in his twenties, he admits the environment he entered was a "trap". At a so-called deal point in a social housing estate - sealed off and controlled by DZ Mafia - price lists for cocaine, hashish and marijuana are graffitied on a wall. The estate acts as a natural fortress for drug dealers. With one major road in and out, they can control the flow of customers and see if the police are coming. It is not uncommon for the sound of automatic gunfire to fill the night air in these areas. After months of negotiations, a deal-point manager from a rival gang agrees to meet us where he works. We enter the estate early in the morning, the birdsong and children walking to school providing a stark contrast to the industrial-scale criminal operation that takes place here. "Joe" says he was making €3,000 (£2,500) a month when he was 13. Now he says that has risen to between €5,000 and €10,000 a month. He seems to see his life path as pre-ordained, albeit a lucrative one. We ask Joe if he thinks about the lives lost because of the violence carried out by his gang, but the 23-year-old has also long made peace with the pain and destruction drug trafficking can cause. "It destroys people, but we all make our own choices," he shrugs. The work that Joe's gang and DZ Mafia are doing represents a threat to national security, says Zoulas, of the anti-drug trafficking unit. There are road accidents, as well as family violence, depressions, suicides and more than 700 overdoses each year, he says, "and it distorts the economy". "We are heading towards a potential systemic breakdown of the criminal justice system." Police have had success in Marseille and other cities against drug gangs. Criminal operations are being frustrated, more kingpins arrested and drugs seized. Since 2024, about 1,000 individuals associated with DZ Mafia have been arrested, and 600 incarcerated, police say. But overall, it is a battle that is becoming more arduous, rather than easier. As gangs seek to widen their operations, or replace members who have been arrested or killed, social media has become a potent recruitment tool - especially since the Covid pandemic, when many street-drug sales jumped online. On social media, we found countless posts advertising jobs in Marseille for aspiring drivers, couriers and hitmen, often with glamourised AI-generated images. Nets are also being cast wider, as it becomes harder to entice young people locally because they know more about what might happen to them. The ads can reach teenagers in most corners of France - including Paris, Nantes and Lille - and serve as a powerful pull to Marseille, and the Quartier Nord, police say. Online advertising has also changed the typical profile of someone who would join a gang's ranks, say law enforcement officials. Now, it is often someone without a criminal past, but who has exploitable vulnerabilities, like having a difficult family life. "These people are recruited by unscrupulous sponsors who send them into the lion's den," explains Thibaut Fontaine, the head of France's anti-organised-crime unit. Their lack of criminal experience, he says, makes them easier to arrest quickly. Karine still has no idea why her son, Hugo, was shot. Asked what she would say to gang leaders recruiting children and young men in Marseille, she says: "They destroy families. Little sisters, little brothers, grandparents. But then, I don't think those people have a heart, really." The restaurant where her son said he was going to work did exist, but staﬀ there told Karine they had never recruited anyone called Hugo. The reason for his death almost certainly lies within Marseille's Quartier Nord. Additional reporting by Marianne Baisnee, Lea Guedj and Paul Pradier

news.summary: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.

news.titleTr: Here’s what happened in crypto today
news.summaryTr: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
news.articleText: Here’s what happened in crypto today Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation. Today in crypto: Zcash developers are seeking another reduction in block times to speed up transaction confirmations, just days after the NU7 upgrade cut the interval from 75 seconds to 25 seconds. Binance France is closing up shop in the country, as all accounts will be closed on Dec. 31, while the US Treasury imposed financial sanctions on eight Canadian money-service companies it claims have done business with sanctioned Iranian entities. Zcash devs propose another block time cut days after NU7 upgrade Zcash developers have proposed reducing the blockchain’s target block interval from 25 seconds to 20 seconds, seeking faster transaction confirmations days after activating the NU7 upgrade. On Sunday, developers ValarDragon and Evan Forbes submitted a draft Zcash Improvement Proposal (ZIP) on GitHub, saying that they want the change to be included in the next community poll and considered for the upcoming NU7.1 network upgrade. The reduction would shorten the expected wait for initial transaction confirmations. According to the proposal, this would improve the user experience for point-of-sale payments, exchange deposits and cross-chain swaps. The developers said the change would not increase the network’s overall daily capacity for private transactions. The proposal would also preserve Zcash’s existing issuance schedule, despite blocks being produced more frequently. The proposal comes just days after Zcash’s NU7 upgrade went live. On Friday, the NU7 upgrade was activated on the mainnet, cutting the network’s target block interval from 75 seconds to 25 seconds. The upgrade also introduced a Network Sustainability Mechanism designed to recycle a portion of transaction fees into future mining rewards while preserving Zcash’s 21 million ZEC supply cap. Binance France emails announce closure of accounts Dec. 31 Binance France is closing up shop in the country. Customers have been notified by email during early November, according to media reports. All accounts will be closed on Dec. 31, and any assets left on the exchange will be charged monthly fees starting on Nov. 29, Cryptoast, Crypto Briefing and other media reported on Saturday, citing emails sent to users by Binance. On that date, accounts still maintaining a balance will pay a monthly maintenance fee of 0.025% of the balance, or a minimum of 10 USDC, a stablecoin tracking the US dollar. To avoid fees, withdrawals must be completed by Nov. 29, the exchange said. US sanctions Canadian money-exchange firms over Iran ties The US Treasury imposed financial sanctions on eight Canadian money-service companies it claims have done business with sanctioned Iranian entities. These companies facilitated the exchange of Iranian rials and other currencies for digital assets, enabling international transactions, a US Treasury Department statement said on Friday. The sanctions, which serve to isolate the companies from the dollar-based financial system, are the latest in a series of Treasury moves against firms outside the US. These businesses have facilitated transactions with sanctioned Iranian digital asset exchanges, as well as with digital asset addresses associated with Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), according to the Treasury.

On Sunday, developers ValarDragon and Evan Forbes submitted a draft Zcash Improvement Proposal (ZIP) on the Zcash community forum, saying that they want the change to be included in the next community poll and considered for the upcoming NU7.1 network upgrade. The reduction would shorten the expected wait for initial transaction confirmations. According to the proposal, this would improve the user experience for point-of-sale payments, exchange deposits and cross-chain swaps. The developers said the change would not increase the network’s overall daily capacity for private transactions. The proposal would also preserve Zcash’s existing issuance schedule, despite blocks being produced more frequently. The proposal comes just days after Zcash’s NU7 upgrade went live. On Friday, the NU7 upgrade was activated on the mainnet, cutting the network’s target block interval from 75 seconds to 25 seconds. The upgrade also introduced a Network Sustainability Mechanism designed to recycle a portion of transaction fees into future mining rewards while preserving Zcash’s 21 million ZEC supply cap. Related: Zcash grants group offers $124M compromise as governance backlash grows

news.summary: Pope Leo made the comments as he arrived in Argentina on the second leg of his Latin America tour.

news.titleTr: Pope delivers veiled rebuke of Milei's austerity measures
news.summaryTr: Pope Leo made the comments as he arrived in Argentina on the second leg of his Latin America tour.
news.articleText: Pope delivers veiled rebuke of Milei's austerity measures - Published Pope Leo XIV has said Argentina's economy must benefit everyone including the poor, in a diplomatic but pointed critique of President Javier Milei's austerity measures. The Pope was speaking as he arrived in Buenos Aires, the second stop on a 12-day tour of Latin America, only three weeks after having had surgery for lung cancer. In response, right-wing leader Milei said his government was working to avoid "punishing the Argentines of tomorrow in order to benefit the Argentines of today". This leg of the Pope's journey was expected be the most politically sensitive, with the president's agenda of slashing public spending having been denounced by the Catholic Church for hitting the poorest hardest. "The economy must be at the service of the people, rather than people being at the service of the economy," Pope Leo said. He stressed the plight of those who, "despite hard work, nonetheless struggle to meet their household's needs", and urged that "particular concern be shown for those affected by illness, dependency and disability" - a veiled reference to the government's controversial cuts to disability assistance. In what appeared to be a rebuke of Milei's combative style and language, the Pope said strengthening democracy required a "willingness to listen" and the "careful use of words". Milei had been particularly outspoken about Leo's predecessor Pope Francis, whom he called "evil on earth" and a "communist" for promoting a doctrine of social justice to help the poor. On Sunday, however, Milei struck a conciliatory tone, calling Francis an "exceptional figure" and "undoubtedly the most important Argentine in history". He was also keen to welcome the current Pope earlier, writing in a post on X that Argentina awaits "with immense joy". Pope Leo urged Argentina to safeguard its democracy. "Those who exercise authority have a duty to act with prudence, to acknowledge the limits of the power entrusted to them, and to direct their decisions toward the good of the entire community," he said. In his own address welcoming Leo to Argentina, Milei defended his libertarian policies, saying the rights to life, liberty and property are the backbone of Argentina's constitution and of Western democracies. The Argentine leader, who has said he will seek re-election next year, is a strong supporter of US President Donald Trump, who has criticised Pope Leo for his opposition to the Iran war. Pope Leo's trip to Argentina has been described as a homage to Francis, who did not return to his homeland during his own papacy. The Vatican says no extraordinary measures are being taken in relation to the Pope's health, describing him as a "71-year-old who has undergone an operation" not someone with a "permanent medical condition". Last month's operation to remove a tumour was successful and his doctors say the cancer has not spread. Related topics - Published6 May 2024 - Published22 April 2025 - Published27 October 2025

news.titleTr: tBTC bridge partially resumes as $120M Aave reserve remains frozen
news.summaryTr: Threshold halted its tBTC bridge on Oct. 30 as operators addressed a critical Linux kernel vulnerability that could allow attackers to execute code on unpatched servers.
news.articleText: tBTC bridge partially resumes as $120M Aave reserve remains frozen Threshold halted its tBTC bridge on Oct. 30 as operators addressed a critical Linux kernel vulnerability that could allow attackers to execute code on unpatched servers. Threshold Network’s tBTC bridge has resumed onchain operations after a nine-day security pause, but an Aave reserve holding about $120 million in tBTC remains frozen to new deposits and borrowing against the token. On Sunday, Threshold said the bridge’s underlying network was restarting as security-patched node operators reconnected. These independent operators collectively authorize Bitcoin movements and process deposits and redemptions. Requests submitted before the shutdown are expected to be processed as more operators return, but the app will not accept new deposits, minting or redemptions until enough nodes are online. Threshold did not announce a restart date. Threshold initially halted the bridge on Oct. 30 while operators addressed a critical Linux kernel vulnerability that could allow remote attackers to execute code on unpatched servers. The project said it found no evidence the flaw was exploited against tBTC nodes. Aave froze its tBTC reserve on Ethereum Core on Oct. 31 to prevent additional exposure while redemptions were unavailable. The restriction stops new tBTC deposits and the token from adding borrowing power, while existing users can still withdraw and repay loans. Threshold said roughly 4,320 BTC remains in bridge wallets against about 4,185 tBTC in circulation, with no unauthorized Bitcoin transfers or token minting detected. Aave risk provider LlamaRisk said it would propose restoring the reserve after Threshold’s operations return to normal. Related: Threshold: Upgraded bridge to funnel $500B institutional BTC into DeFi

news.title: CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation
news.articleText: Release Number 9323-26 CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation November 05, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today issued an interpretation (“Interpretation”) of the requirement that designated contract markets (“DCMs”) provide competitive, open, fair, and impartial access to their members and persons with trading privileges under Commission Regulation 38.151(b) (“Impartial Access Requirements”). “Derivatives markets must operate on a uniform basis at a national scale in order to achieve the purposes set out in the Commodity Exchange Act,” said Chairman Michael S. Selig. “Geographic access restrictions are inconsistent with those purposes and the Act’s impartial access requirements.” DCMs must cease domestic geographic restrictions that violate the Impartial Access Requirements within 30 days, or else submit to the Division of Market Oversight (“Division”) an explanation for why such compliance is not feasible. Further, within 30 days, DCMs should ensure that intermediaries accessing their markets are not impeding and are complying with the DCM’s Impartial Access Requirements, or else submit to the Division an explanation for why such compliance is not feasible. The Commission will consider the facts and circumstances of any particular case in connection with potential Commission action. -CFTC-

news.articleText: Release Number 9322-26 CFTC Staff Addresses Use of Trust Companies for Daily Settlements November 05, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission’s Division of Clearing and Risk today issued a no-action letter addressing whether derivatives clearing organizations may use trust companies to conduct daily settlements with clearing members. According to the letter, a derivatives clearing organization may use a trust company for daily settlements if it treats the trust company as it would a settlement bank under applicable CFTC requirements. -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets
news.articleText: Release Number 9321-26 CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets November 04, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the U.S. Department of Agriculture today announced their signing of a Memorandum of Understanding intended to safeguard the integrity of U.S. agricultural markets. The MOU will allow the CFTC and USDA to harmonize policies and practices to better share information and increase access to risk management tools. The agreement will also assist both agencies with monitoring and identifying structural or potential systematic risks, among other things. “For decades, America’s agricultural community has relied on our markets to hedge risk, manage uncertainty, and plan for the future,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig. “I’m proud that the CFTC and USDA have formalized this partnership through an MOU that will strengthen protections for America’s farmers, ranchers, and producers while expanding opportunities to manage risk through more efficient data sharing. I commend Secretary Rollins for her partnership and commitment to a more coordinated regulatory approach that safeguards the integrity of our markets and ensures they continue serving the agricultural community that feeds and clothes our nation.” “Faster and more transparent data sharing between USDA and CFTC is critical to helping our farmers and ranchers navigate an ever-changing market,” said USDA Secretary Brooke Rollins. “This MOU builds upon USDA’s ongoing data modernization efforts and allows our agencies to collaboratively identify risks and improve responses to market events. Breaking down barriers between government agencies to deliver for our customers is a hallmark of this administration and I am looking forward to the successes this MOU will bring.” -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud
news.articleText: Release Number 9320-26 CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud November 03, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Texas entered a default judgment against defendants Walter Dunning Larrick III and Cambridge Financial Advisors LLC for their participation in a commodities fraud scheme. In entering the default judgment, the court found the defendants fraudulently solicited and misappropriated more than $3 million from participants. The court found the defendants falsely represented they would use participant funds to trade futures and options, including those involving natural gas, oil, and gold; made material misrepresentations and omissions about the profitability of commodity trading with them; and issued false account statements to conceal their misconduct. The court further found the defendants misappropriated participant funds by making payments to existing participants in a manner akin to a Ponzi scheme, paying Larrick’s personal expenses, and sending funds to offshore accounts in Costa Rica. The court ordered the defendants to pay a $9,767,625 civil monetary penalty and $3,255,875 in restitution. It also permanently enjoined them from further violations of the Commodity Exchange Act and Commission regulations, as charged, and imposed permanent trading and registration bans. The default judgment resolves all claims in the CFTC’s 2023 complaint. [See CFTC Press Release No. 8768-23.] -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures
news.articleText: Release Number 9319-26 CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures November 03, 2026 WASHINGTON — CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig today released a statement announcing that perpetual futures contracts on individual equity securities can begin trading for the first time on designated contract markets that are dually registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission as notice-registered national securities exchanges to trade security futures products. Key excerpts from Chairman Selig’s statement: “Today, perpetual futures contracts on individual equity securities (the ‘Equity Perps’) can begin trading for the first time on CFTC-registered exchanges. … “This expansion marks a significant step towards allowing U.S. market participants, consistent with applicable law, to avail themselves of the advantages of perpetual futures that have led to their emergence as widely sought tools for risk-management and price-discovery. I believe that bringing these types of innovative products into our regulated markets ensures that American investors and traders can access these products within the protections of the CFTC’s proven regulatory framework, rather than being forced to turn to offshore, and often unregulated, venues. … “The Equity Perps build on the foundation of the [Commodity Futures Modernization Act of 2000] and the [CFTC-SEC Memorandum of Understanding]. For too long, regulatory uncertainty left innovative products, such as security futures and equity perpetual futures, stranded in what SEC Chairman Paul S. Atkins has aptly described as a regulatory ‘no man’s land’ due to a lack of harmonization between the agencies. The CFTC and SEC have turned the page on that era, and are committed to delivering regulatory clarity for innovative products and a clear path to market, rather than more casualties of jurisdictional disputes.” Read Chairman Selig’s full statement here. -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
news.articleText: Release Number 9318-26 CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading October 28, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced it will host an industry roundtable Dec. 15 to discuss issues related to the viability of derivatives markets moving to 24/7 trading. The dialogue will build upon the CFTC’s Request for Comment earlier this summer on 24/7 trading. The CFTC’s roundtable will provide a public venue for dialogue on the evolving market structures shaping derivatives markets, including overnight trading, tokenization, infrastructure and staffing needs, and operational readiness. Participants will convene from across the industry to discuss how the Commission can promote responsible innovation while protecting market participants and preserving the integrity and resilience of U.S. derivatives markets. “I have been consistently clear: under my leadership, the CFTC will not take a one‑size‑fits‑all approach to 24/7 trading. Market structure evolves best through thoughtful and responsible progress, and that’s exactly why we’re hosting a roundtable to hear directly from industry on their views for 24/7 trading across different asset classes,” Chairman Selig said. The roundtable will take place at CFTC’s headquarters in Washington. Information regarding the agenda, speakers, and registration will be posted at a later date. This event will be open to the public and livestreamed on CFTC.gov. Please note the number of in-person participants may be limited, and visitors will be subject to security checks. Members of the public are welcome to submit speaker nominations to [email protected]. -CFTC-
news.articleTextTr: Release Number 9318-26 CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading October 28, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced it will host an industry roundtable Dec. 15 to discuss issues related to the viability of derivatives markets moving to 24/7 trading. The dialogue will build upon the CFTC’s Request for Comment earlier this summer on 24/7 trading. The CFTC’s roundtable will provide a public venue for dialogue on the evolving market structures shaping derivatives markets, including overnight trading, tokenization, infrastructure and staffing needs, and operational readiness. Participants will convene from across the industry to discuss how the Commission can promote responsible innovation while protecting market participants and preserving the integrity and resilience of U.S. derivatives markets. “I have been consistently clear: under my leadership, the CFTC will not take a one‑size‑fits‑all approach to 24/7 trading. news.title: ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026
news.articleText: Release Number 9317-26 ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026 October 27, 2026 WASHINGTON — Last week, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the Risk Management Center at Kansas State University co-hosted the 2026 Agricultural Commodity Futures Conference (AgCon) in Overland Park, Kansas. The two-day conference brought together industry leaders, policymakers, and market participants to examine critical issues facing the agricultural economy, developments in derivatives markets, and the risk management tools American farmers, ranchers, and agribusinesses depend on. Conference Highlights CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig joined K-State President Richard Linton to welcome participants on opening day. CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig addressed conference attendees, “I have spent a lot of time this year traveling around the country and talking to farmers and ranchers working hard each day to provide the food, feed, and fiber we depend on throughout our country and the world. I’ve met with farmers, ranchers, agribusinesses, and energy producers in Iowa, Texas, Nebraska, South Carolina, and Florida, and now, I’m with all of you here in Kansas.” [Watch Chairman Selig’s full remarks here.] Following Chairman Selig’s remarks, panelists examined the relationship between cash and derivatives markets, evolving commodity contracts, and the importance of effective hedging tools for agricultural producers. There were also panels where industry representatives addressed access to agricultural credit and the financial challenges facing producers and merchants. Additional afternoon discussions focused on rising production costs, fluctuating commodity prices, supply chain disruptions, and broader pressures on the farm economy. In addition, conference participants engaged in discussions about emerging market developments, including perpetual futures, 24/7 trading, and tokenized collateral, and their implications for agricultural risk management. CFTC Chief Advisor Alex Titus and White House Council of Economic Advisers Member Aaron Hedlund also examined the U.S. economic outlook, agricultural trade, and policies shaping American agriculture. The first day concluded with a keynote address from U.S. Department of Agriculture Deputy Secretary Stephen Vaden. U.S. Senator Roger Marshall of Kansas opened the second day with a morning keynote address on agricultural policy and legislative priorities facing American producers. The morning continued with discussions on agricultural prediction markets, the use of data in modern commodity markets, and developments in event contracts. In addition, panelists examined superintelligence, information advantages, and market integrity, including the implications of emerging technologies for market participants and regulators. Chairman Selig joined Futures Industry Association President and CEO Walt Lukken for a fireside chat examining the Commission’s priorities, the evolving regulatory landscape, and developments shaping derivatives markets. The conference concluded with discussions on enhancing public understanding of markets through data and customer education, followed by a panel examining clearing, market access, and the role of intermediaries in derivatives markets. Chairman Selig delivered closing remarks, concluding AgCon2026. -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC Announces Semiweekly Publication of the COT Report
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC Announces Semiweekly Publication of the COT Report
news.articleText: Release Number 9316-26 CFTC Announces Semiweekly Publication of the COT Report October 27, 2026 WASHINGTON — CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig announced the CFTC’s plan to increase the publication frequency of the Commitments of Traders Report (COT Report) from once to twice a week by the end of 2026. Data from Monday will be published on Wednesday, and data from Wednesday will be published on Friday. Both reports will be released at 3:30 p.m. ET on their respective publication days. Under the enhanced publication schedule, the reports’ latency will decrease from three days to two days. The change follows the Commission’s recent Request for Comment and reflects its commitment to providing market participants with more timely information about trading positions and activity in agricultural markets. The CFTC’s Division of Data is leading the effort to operationalize the expanded publication schedule through modernization and automation while maintaining accuracy. “COT Reports have been an important source of transparency for decades. Following feedback from the agricultural community, I’m pleased to announce the CFTC will be rolling out COT Reports twice a week to ensure this information stream is as useful as possible,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig. -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC Sues to Block State Enforcement in Utah Amid Ongoing Efforts to Preserve Jurisdiction
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC Sues to Block State Enforcement in Utah Amid Ongoing Efforts to Preserve Jurisdiction
news.articleText: Release Number 9315-26 CFTC Sues to Block State Enforcement in Utah Amid Ongoing Efforts to Preserve Jurisdiction October 27, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission announced today it has filed a lawsuit against Utah to block the state’s efforts to shut down CFTC-registered contract markets using state laws. The lawsuit follows Utah’s decision to file civil enforcement actions in state court against CFTC-regulated markets and other businesses. Utah’s effort to restrict the functioning of CFTC-registered exchanges obstructs Congress’s decision to federally preempt state law. “Utah seeks to shut down prediction markets across a wide variety of markets,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig. “Event contracts do not just serve hedging and investment purposes—they also provide the public with information about the outcome of future events. Congress entrusted the CFTC to be the federal regulator with sole responsibility to oversee these markets. As I’ve said before, the CFTC has the expertise and responsibility to defend its exclusive jurisdiction over commodity derivatives, and that’s exactly what we’ll do.” This action reflects the CFTC’s firm commitment to maintaining its exclusive jurisdiction over CFTC-registered prediction markets. The CFTC continues to draw a clear line: if a state challenges the lawful operation of a derivatives exchange, the Commission will protect federal sovereign interests. The Commission has also initiated legal proceedings against nine other states and has submitted briefs in four federal courts of appeal and one state supreme court. -CFTC-

items.articleText: Borsa İstanbul'da dip oluşuyor mu? İki uzmandan yükseliş sinyali Borsa İstanbul'da yaşanan düzeltmenin ardından toparlanma beklentileri güçleniyor. CNBC-e yayınında piyasaları değerlendiren iki uzman, satış baskısı ve dip oluşumuna ilişkin görüşlerini paylaşırken, yükselişin devamı için öne çıkan hedefleri açıkladı. CNBC-e canlı yayınında Şafak Tükle'nin sorularını yanıtlayan Marbaş Menkul Değerler Genel Müdür Yardımcısı Sertaç Ekeke, Borsa İstanbul'da düzeltme hareketinin ardından tepki yükselişinin yaşandığını söyledi. 11.300 üzerindeki kapanışların önemli olduğunu belirten Ekeke, endekste 11.300 ve 11.700 seviyelerini destek noktaları olarak değerlendirdi. Ekeke, 11 Kasım'da açıklanacak MSCI kararının da piyasalar açısından yakından izleneceğini ifade etti. One Portföy Fon Yöneticisi Cenk Akyoldaş ise borsada taban oluşumunun başladığını belirterek derinleşen satış baskısı görmediğini söyledi. Akyoldaş, 10.650 seviyesinin aşılması halinde 11.563-11.955 bandının gündeme gelebileceğini, kendi hedefinin ise 12.250 olduğunu dile getirdi. Akyoldaş, 41.000-41.250 aralığını önemli direnç bölgesi olarak değerlendirdi. MSCI değerlendirmesi neden önemli? MSCI (Morgan Stanley Capital International), küresel yatırımcıların takip ettiği hisse senedi endekslerini hazırlıyor. 11 Kasım'da açıklanacak endeks değerlendirmesi, Borsa İstanbul'daki bazı şirketlerin MSCI endekslerine dahil edilmesi, çıkarılması veya ağırlıklarının değiştirilmesi açısından önem taşıyor.

items.summary: Halkbank, KOBİ'lerin yeşil ve sosyal dönüşümünü desteklemek amacıyla 31 kredi ve destek ürününü kapsayan 100 milyar liralık finansman paketi hazırladı. Bankanın sürdürülebilir finansman ve sosyal kalkınma katkısı ise 424 milyar liraya ulaştı.

items.titleTr: Halkbank COP31 için hazırladı: KOBİ'lere 100 milyar TL finansman
items.summaryTr: Halkbank, KOBİ'lerin yeşil ve sosyal dönüşümünü desteklemek amacıyla 31 kredi ve destek ürününü kapsayan 100 milyar liralık finansman paketi hazırladı. Bankanın sürdürülebilir finansman ve sosyal kalkınma katkısı ise 424 milyar liraya ulaştı.
items.articleText: Halkbank COP31 için hazırladı: KOBİ'lere 100 milyar TL finansman - Halkbank, KOBİ'lerin yeşil ve sosyal dönüşümünü desteklemek amacıyla 31 kredi ve destek ürününü kapsayan 100 milyar liralık finansman paketi hazırladı. Bankanın sürdürülebilir finansman ve sosyal kalkınma katkısı ise 424 milyar liraya ulaştı. Halkbank, Birleşmiş Milletler İklim Değişikliği Çerçeve Sözleşmesi 31. Taraflar Konferansı'na (COP31) özel olarak KOBİ'lerin çevresel, sosyal ve ekonomik dönüşümünü desteklemek amacıyla 100 milyar TL büyüklüğünde finansman paketi hazırladı. 31 kredi ve destek ürününü bir araya getiriyor CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Bir kısmı Kredi Garanti Fonu (KGF) destekli olan KOBİ Sürdürülebilir Dönüşüm Paketi, 3 ana finansman ekseninde 31 kredi ve destek ürününü bir araya getiriyor. Paket kapsamında farklı vade ve faiz koşullarıyla KOBİ'lerin ihtiyaçlarına yönelik finansman çözümleri sunulması hedefleniyor. Halkbank Genel Müdürü Recep Süleyman Özdil, paketin işletmelerin değişen koşullara uyum sağlamasına, rekabet gücünü artırmasına ve sürdürülebilir büyümesine katkı sunmasını amaçladıklarını belirtti. Yenilenebilir enerji, düşük karbonlu üretim, döngüsel ekonomi, enerji ve kaynak verimliliği gibi alanlarda finansman desteğini artırdıklarını aktaran Özdil, genç ve kadın girişimciler başta olmak üzere esnaf ve KOBİ'lerin finansmana erişimini önceliklendireceklerini ifade etti. Yeşil dönüşüm ve sosyal kalkınmaya 424 milyar TL katkı Özdil, sürdürülebilir finansman kapsamında yenilenebilir enerji tesislerinin kurulması, enerji verimliliğinin artırılması, atıkların geri dönüştürülmesi, su kaynaklarının korunması ve elektrikli araç şarj altyapısının geliştirilmesi gibi alanlarda finansman imkânları sunduklarını bildirdi. Yeşil dönüşüm ve sosyal kalkınmaya sağladıkları katkının 2026 itibarıyla 424 milyar TL'ye ulaştığını belirten Özdil, bu tutarın bankanın toplam nakdi kredilerinin yüzde 16'sını oluşturduğunu kaydetti. Halkbank'ın bağlı ortaklığı Halk Elektrik Üretim AŞ tarafından Karaman'da kurulması planlanan 100 megavat kapasiteli depolamalı güneş enerjisi santraline de değinen Özdil, projenin yaklaşık 120 bin hanenin yıllık elektrik ihtiyacına karşılık gelen miktarda enerji üretmesinin hedeflendiğini aktardı. Santralin yılda 175 bin ton karbon emisyonunu önlemesinin öngörüldüğünü belirten Özdil, bunun yaklaşık 3 milyon ağacın yıllık karbon tutumuna eşdeğer çevresel fayda sağlayacağını ifade etti. COP31'de sürdürülebilir finansman panelleri düzenlenecek Halkbank, Türkiye'nin ev sahipliğinde Antalya'da düzenlenecek COP31 kapsamında iklim finansmanı, yenilenebilir enerji, kurumsal risk yönetimi ve kapsayıcı büyüme konularındaki deneyimini paylaşacak. Zirvenin Mavi Bölge'sinde düzenlenecek “Geleceği Finanse Etmek: Sürdürülebilir Finans, Dönüşüm ve Kapsayıcı Büyüme” oturumunda finans sektörünün dönüşüm sürecindeki rolü ele alınacak. Yeşil Bölge'de ise “Megawatt'tan Megadeğere”, “Kadınların Güçlendirilmesi” ve “İklim Riski Bilançoya Nasıl Girer?” başlıklı panellerde sürdürülebilir enerji, toplumsal cinsiyet eşitliği, iklim risklerinin finansal etkileri ve yeşil dönüşümün finansmanı değerlendirilecek.

Santralin yılda 175 bin ton karbon emisyonunu önlemesinin öngörüldüğünü belirten Özdil, bunun yaklaşık 3 milyon ağacın yıllık karbon tutumuna eşdeğer çevresel fayda sağlayacağını ifade etti. COP31'de sürdürülebilir finansman panelleri düzenlenecek Halkbank, Türkiye'nin ev sahipliğinde Antalya'da düzenlenecek COP31 kapsamında iklim finansmanı, yenilenebilir enerji, kurumsal risk yönetimi ve kapsayıcı büyüme konularındaki deneyimini paylaşacak. Zirvenin Mavi Bölge'sinde düzenlenecek “Geleceği Finanse Etmek: Sürdürülebilir Finans, Dönüşüm ve Kapsayıcı Büyüme” oturumunda finans sektörünün dönüşüm sürecindeki rolü ele alınacak. Yeşil Bölge'de ise “Megawatt'tan Megadeğere”, “Kadınların Güçlendirilmesi” ve “İklim Riski Bilançoya Nasıl Girer?” başlıklı panellerde sürdürülebilir enerji, toplumsal cinsiyet eşitliği, iklim risklerinin finansal etkileri ve yeşil dönüşümün finansmanı değerlendirilecek.

items.articleText: Avrupa'da emeklilik için ne kadar birikim gerekiyor? OECD verilerine göre, 30 Avrupa ülkesinin 22'sinde zorunlu emeklilik sistemi brüt maaşın yüzde 70'i kadar gelir sağlamadığı aktarıldı. Emeklilik hedefi için gereken aylık ek tasarruf Türkiye'de 5 euro, İsviçre'de 1.084 euro olarak hesaplandı. Ekonomik İşbirliği ve Kalkınma Örgütü (OECD) verilerine göre, incelenen 30 Avrupa ülkesinin 22'sinde zorunlu emeklilik sistemlerinin çalışanlara emeklilik döneminde brüt maaşlarının yüzde 70'i düzeyinde gelir sağlaması beklenmediği belirtildi. Bu nedenle çalışanların, zorunlu primlerine ek olarak gönüllü emeklilik planlarına tasarruf ayırması gerektiği vurgulandı. Euronews Business'ın OECD'nin Pensions Outlook 2026 raporuna dayandırdığı analizde, ortalama ücret alan kadın ve erkek çalışanların emeklilik döneminde hedeflenen gelir düzeyine ulaşabilmesi için kariyerleri boyunca yapmaları gereken ek birikim hesaplandı. OECD, zorunlu emeklilik katkılarına ilave olarak gönüllü emeklilik planlarına aktarılması gereken gelir payını “katkı açığı” olarak tanımlıyor. Katkı açığı Litvanya'da yüzde 20,7'ye çıkıyor Erkek çalışanlar arasında katkı açığının gelire oranı Litvanya'da yüzde 20,7 ile en yüksek seviyeye ulaşıyor. Bu oran İrlanda'da yüzde 19,4, Polonya'da yüzde 17,3, Hırvatistan'da yüzde 15,7, Slovenya'da yüzde 12,5, Letonya'da yüzde 12,3 ve Estonya'da yüzde 12,2 olarak hesaplanıyor. İsviçre'de yüzde 12,1, Almanya'da yüzde 11,1, Belçika'da yüzde 10,7 ve İzlanda'da yüzde 10 düzeyinde bulunan katkı açığı, İngiltere'de yüzde 9,1, Fransa'da yüzde 6,2 olarak ölçülüyor. Türkiye ise yüzde 0,4 ile pozitif katkı açığının en düşük olduğu ülke konumunda. Bulgaristan'da bu oran yüzde 4,4, Slovakya'da yüzde 3,9 ve İsveç'te yüzde 2,2 seviyesinde bulunuyor. Avusturya, Danimarka, Yunanistan, İtalya, Lüksemburg, Hollanda, Portekiz ve İspanya'da ise ortalama ücret alan erkek çalışanların zorunlu emeklilik sisteminden elde edecekleri gelirin OECD'nin yüzde 70'lik hedefini karşılaması bekleniyor. İsviçre'de aylık ek birikim 1.084 euro Euronews Business, OECD'nin katkı açığı oranlarını 2025 yılı ortalama brüt ücretlerine uygulayarak çalışanların ayda ne kadar ek tasarruf yapması gerektiğini hesapladı. Buna göre, ortalama ücret alan erkek çalışanların emeklilik hedefini karşılamak için ayırması gereken ek tutar Türkiye'de aylık yaklaşık 5 eurodan İsviçre'de 1.084 euroya kadar değişiyor. İsviçre'nin ardından İrlanda 974 euro, İzlanda 716 euro, Almanya 617 euro, Belçika 556 euro ve Norveç 532 euro ile aylık ek birikim ihtiyacının 500 euroyu aştığı ülkeler arasında yer alıyor. İngiltere'de ortalama ücretli bir erkeğin ayda yaklaşık 494 euro, Polonya'da 360 euro, Fransa'da 238 euro ek tasarruf yapması gerekiyor. Bu tutar Macaristan'da 129 euro, Romanya'da 111 euro, İsveç'te 91 euro, Bulgaristan'da 68 euro ve Slovakya'da 64 euro olarak hesaplanıyor. Türkiye'de ortalama brüt ücret 1.549 euro Ülkeler arasındaki farkta ücret düzeyleri de etkili oluyor. 2025 yılında ortalama brüt aylık kazanç Türkiye'de 1.549 euro, İsviçre'de ise 8.957 euro olarak hesaplandı. Almanya'da 5.558 euro, İngiltere'de 5.445 euro, İsveç'te 4.195 euro, Fransa'da 3.830 euro, Polonya'da 2.078 euro ve Macaristan'da 1.772 euro seviyesinde bulunuyor. Bu ücretler üzerinden hesaplandığında, emeklilik gelirinin brüt kazancın yüzde 70'ine ulaşması Türkiye'de aylık yaklaşık 1.084 euro, İsviçre'de ise 6.270 euro gelir anlamına geliyor. OECD Politika Analisti Stéphanie Payet, katkı açığının ülkelerin zorunlu emeklilik sistemlerinden sağladığı gelirle doğrudan bağlantılı olduğunu belirtti. Payet'e göre, zorunlu emeklilik sisteminin maaşı karşılama oranı düştükçe çalışanların hedeflenen emeklilik gelirine ulaşmak için gönüllü tasarruflarını artırması gerekiyor.
